canonical.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
canonical.sourceFilePath: 08. Sliding Window/1. Medium Problems/08. Maximum Points you can obtaln form the card.cpp

narrative.title: The Dispatch Queue Card Pickup
narrative.scenario: A dispatch console shows a row of task cards, each carrying a completion score. An operator must claim exactly k cards but may only take from the two ends of the row. Because the claimed cards always form one prefix glued to one suffix, the unclaimed middle is a single contiguous block — and minimizing that block's score maximizes the haul.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array cardPoints and an integer k, the number of cards to claim.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum total score obtainable by claiming k cards from the row's ends.

testCases.explanation: Claiming 1+6+5 from the ends beats any other split of three picks.
All cards score alike, so any two picks yield the same total.

starterCode.python:
def max_score(card_points, k):
    total = sum(card_points)
    keep = len(card_points) - k          # cards left unclaimed form a block
    window = sum(card_points[:keep])
    best = window
    for i in range(keep, len(card_points)):
        window += card_points[i] - card_points[i - keep]
        best = min(best, window)
    return total - best

hintLevels: Level 1: Taking k from the ends equals leaving one contiguous block of n-k cards behind.
Level 2: Slide a fixed-size window of length n-k and minimize its sum.
Level 3: Answer is total minus that minimum — careful when k equals n (the block is empty).
